terms.meaning: pictures of land taken from above, such as satellite photos
a number that summarises one kind of change, such as vegetation
the difference between two percentages, such as going from 40 percent to 45 percent
a record of where a piece of data came from

used_by: Reason not stated in the code. Likely the imagery and screen code, not shown in the packet.

sections.name: ImageryProviderName, ImagerySourceType, ImageryQuality, ImageryVisualVariant, EarthObservationIndicatorType
sections.title: Imagery and change labels
sections.what: Lists the allowed names for the imagery provider, source, quality, visual look, indicator type, and how a change is classified.
sections.why: Fixed labels keep the change results consistent and clearly marked as demonstration only.
sections.watch_out: The provider and source names are fixed to synthetic values, so a real provider needs new labels.

sections.name: ImagerySnapshot
sections.title: One imagery snapshot
sections.what: Describes one picture: its id, the case, the date, where it came from, its reference, its quality and look, optional measurements, and a note. It is always marked synthetic and not authoritative.
sections.why: The fixed synthetic and not-authoritative flags keep demo pictures from being treated as official.
sections.watch_out: The metrics are optional, so code must handle a snapshot that has none.

sections.name: EarthObservationIndicator
sections.title: One change indicator
sections.what: Describes one measured change: the earlier and later values, the difference in percentage points, the classification, the explanation key, and the quality.
sections.why: Separating the raw values from the classification lets screens explain the result in plain words.
sections.watch_out: Earlier, later and difference can be empty, so a missing measurement must not be shown as zero.

sections.name: EarthObservationInsight
sections.title: Overall insight for a parcel
sections.what: Describes the full result for one parcel: its snapshots, all its indicators, the overall classification, the thresholds used, and the safety flags that mark it synthetic and not legal evidence.
sections.why: Bundling the policy thresholds with the result means anyone can see how the classification was decided.
sections.watch_out: The provenance can be a no-fixture value, so the screen should say that no imagery was available rather than show empty results.

summary: Defines the shapes for satellite-style imagery snapshots and the change indicators calculated from them.
purpose: Describes imagery snapshots, indicators of change such as vegetation or built-up area, and the overall insight for a parcel. It marks all of it as synthetic and not legal evidence.
why: Keeping the labels explicit stops demo imagery from being read as authoritative. Likely reason: the safety flags exist so the output is not used as proof. Reason not stated in the code.
how: The file defines the allowed provider names, quality levels, indicator types and classifications. It then defines a snapshot, an indicator with its earlier and later values, and an insight that gathers them with the policy thresholds.
inputs: None directly. Other code fills these shapes.
outputs: None directly. The labels guide the checker and the screens.
risks: The safety flags are only labels. Code that ignores them could present synthetic results as real.
debug: If an insight looks wrong, check the threshold values in the policy block and confirm the provenance fields say synthetic.
